verdict.root_cause: cartservice is not running. Its logs end with a clean application shutdown at ~20:39:40 and produce nothing thereafter, coinciding with a platform-automation image-reference update to the v1.2.1-cartservice-hotfix.2 tag at 20:39:41 [tr_7b57d562352b, tr_059e08eac79c]. The replacement workload never came back up. Every failing checkout trace terminates at checkoutservice's outbound CartService/GetCart span — the deepest and first errored span — failing in ~2-3ms with no fan-out to any other dependency and propagating ERROR up to the frontend [tr_a600c8d24b9b]. That fast-fail profile is the signature of an unavailable endpoint, not a slow or erroring handler, and checkoutservice itself keeps serving normally with no changes and no error logs [tr_eca59f9bf8dc, tr_db596185663b]. The same hotfix tag had been applied and reverted five times in the window, an unstable rollout loop [tr_7b57d562352b]. The artifact that should be serving carts is not serving, so checkout cannot complete an order.
verdict.reasoning: Traces localise the fault below checkoutservice: GetCart is the deepest errored span in all 40 failing traces, and no payment/shipping/currency/catalog/email spans exist, excluding those as origins and excluding checkoutservice's own logic, whose parent span carries no error [tr_a600c8d24b9b]. checkoutservice has no recorded changes and no error or crash evidence, so it is the noticer [tr_db596185663b, tr_eca59f9bf8dc]. On cartservice the mechanism is absence: shutdown at 20:39:40, zero log output at 20:43:15, so requests fail outside a running process; the millisecond latencies rule out a Redis stall or timeout [tr_059e08eac79c, tr_a600c8d24b9b]. The change log ties that shutdown to an image-reference update one second earlier and records no config edits or flag flips [tr_7b57d562352b]. Fix is restoring the last known-good image and confirming readiness, not re-running a tag that has already flapped five times.
open_questions: No container-runtime evidence: restart counts, exit codes, OOM kills, image-pull errors and readiness state for cartservice pods are unobserved, so 'never started' vs 'crash-looping' vs 'image pull failure' is unresolved.
cartservice emits no calls_total series in either incident or baseline windows, an instrumentation gap predating the incident, so its health cannot be confirmed from metrics at all [tr_4f516e08a1f8].
The ~3.5 minute gap between shutdown (20:39:40) and alert onset (20:43:15) is unexplained, and the cartservice log window is truncated from ~20:18 to ~20:39 [tr_059e08eac79c].

alternatives.root_cause: The hotfix.2 cartservice container starts but is immediately killed for exceeding a memory limit, leaving no ready instance to answer GetCart.
alternatives.why_not: Unfalsified rather than supported — no container memory or restart data was collected. The retained logs show one clean shutdown with no subsequent startup attempt, which fits 'never came up' better than a repeating start-and-die cycle.

alternatives.root_cause: cartservice is up but its Redis backing store or service endpoint is unreachable, causing instant connection refusals surfaced as GetCart errors.
alternatives.why_not: Redis connected successfully with a passing test at startup and no connection-failure lines appear; more decisively, cartservice logged nothing at all at the failure time, so no handler was running to reach Redis [tr_059e08eac79c].

proposal.expected_effect: Redeploying cartservice at its prior image tag should bring a serving process back. Observable as: cart-service Loki lines resuming within ~60s with the startup sequence seen at 20:17:57 ('Successfully connected to Redis', 'Initialization completed') where the stream is currently silent after the 20:39:40 shutdown; and checkoutservice's CartService/GetCart spans in Jaeger ceasing to error, with traces continuing past prepareOrderItemsAndShippingQuoteFromCart into the fan-out currently absent. cartservice emits no calls_total series at all, so its own metrics cannot confirm recovery — judge on logs and traces.
proposal.if_wrong: Falsified if no cartservice log lines appear within ~2 minutes (image-pull failure or crash before logging), or startup lines appear then stop again within minutes (crash loop not fixed by the tag), or GetCart keeps failing in ~2-3ms while cartservice logs show a healthy process (fault is upstream of the container). Also treat as wrong if platform-automation re-applies hotfix.2 within minutes — the rollout loop would overwrite this, and pausing that automation is outside what this system may do.
proposal.risk: All five recorded states reference the same hotfix.2 tag, so the 'prior' image is not a known-good artifact and may carry the same defect. If the outage is actually redis-cart, host resources, or a bad container spec, this recreate buys nothing and adds another unexplained transition to a timeline already missing the 20:18-20:39 logs. In-process cart cache is discarded.
proposal.blast_radius: cartservice only, for the recreate duration. checkoutservice is the named inbound caller and sees connection resets — its GetCart calls already fail, so marginal harm is small. frontend and loadgenerator see it transitively.

triage_judgement.reasoning: Critical alerts hitting checkout and frontend simultaneously, with loadgenerator reflecting user-facing impact, cannot be dismissed. No open incidents to attribute this to, and the alerts alone don't distinguish a bad deploy from a failing downstream dependency.
